dublinCore.dc:rights: Pursuant to Title 17 Section 105 of the United States Code, this file is not subject to copyright protection and is in the public domain.

action.action-desc: Mr. Gill of Texas (for himself, Mr. Fine, Ms. Boebert, Mr. Self, Mr. Moore of Alabama, Mr. Perry, and Mr. Norman) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Agriculture

form.official-title: To amend the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 to abolish the restaurant meals program under the supplemental nutrition assistance program.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Ending Restaurant Purchases with SNAP Act of 2026.
The Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 (7 U.S.C. 2011 et seq.) is amended—

subparagraph.text: in paragraph (3), by striking private establishments that contract with the appropriate agency of the State to offer meals for such persons at concessional prices subject to section 9(h),;
in paragraph (4), by striking or by a private establishment that contracts with the appropriate State agency to perform such services at concessional prices subject to section 9(h),; and
in paragraph (9), by striking and by private establishments that contract with the appropriate agency of the State to offer meals for such individuals at concessional prices subject to section 9(h);
in subparagraph (A), by striking (including restaurants participating in a State option restaurant program intended to serve the elderly, disabled, and homeless); and
in subparagraph (B)(ii), by striking , other than restaurants participating in a State option restaurant program;
by redesignating subsections (i) and (j) as subsections (h) and (i), respectively; and

section.text: This Act and the amendments made by this Act shall take effect 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act.
